verdict.rationale: Dynadot's own API page says the API can "programmatically manage domains, account settings, DNS," so DNS automation is a documented first-party capability. The evidence never shows record-level create, update, or delete operations, and the MCP server only claims to "Review nameservers and DNS records." Missing for 10: documented per-record create/update/delete endpoints, TXT-record handling for ACME challenges, a published API reference or OpenAPI spec (all OpenAPI probes returned 404), and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, DNS records are CRUD-able via a documented API — create, update, and delete records programmatically for automation and ACME challenges

citations.quote: The Dynadot API lets you programmatically manage domains, account settings, DNS, orders, and other account activities.
